item_title: Scale-up economics for cultured meat (Humbird 2021; funded by Open Philanthropy)
scope_note: Cultivated meat cost and scale-up (T8, section 10.8)
vietnam_angle: Indirect: Vietnam has no food cell line; the model assumes an engineered, metabolically efficient line and cheap hydrolysate media
vietnam_evidence: None in the paper. Study: no Vietnamese fish or shrimp food cell line (SCI-10; RD-01)
verdict_note: Study figures (USD 37 and 51 per kg wet cells; USD 663 million for 6.9 kt a year) are right. Not yet used: Humbird's own affordability target (about USD 25 per kg of bulk cells, about USD 50 per kg at the shelf), the hydrolysate case (USD 22 per kg) and the asymptote (about USD 16 per kg). Amino acids (USD 19 per kg) outweigh growth factors (USD 3 per kg) at scale, so T8's research focus should include hydrolysate media, not only growth factors v0.10 reconciliation: a commissioned contract, not one of the 61 listed grants (CGG-19).
signal_to_watch: A peer-reviewed food-grade hydrolysate medium that supports fish or bovine cells over many passages
